```{r}

```

```{r historical average}
h <- 5  # 1 = daily, 5 = weekly, 20 = monthly
n <- nrow(df)
r <- df$close_usd_per_troy_oz

# Construct h-step-ahead log return
ytar <- c(r[-h], NA)

U <- which(!is.na(ytar))
X   <- as.matrix(df[U, ])
y   <- ytar[U]
dts <- df$date[U]
Nu <- length(y)

ha <- c(rep(NA, h), cumsum(y)[seq_len(Nu - h)] / seq_len(Nu - h))

val_idx  <- which(dts >= val_start & dts < test_start)
test_idx <- which(dts >= test_start)
ev_idx <- c(val_idx, test_idx)

cat(sprintf("Target: %d-day-ahead gold raw price | ", h))
cat(sprintf(
  "Origins %s -> %s | N=%d | p=%d | train %d | val %d | test %d\n",
  dts[1], dts[length(dts)], length(y), ncol(X), val_idx[1] - 1, length(val_idx),
  length(test_idx)))
```

```{r}
runrlasso <- function(df, indice, pl=FALSE) {
  
  train <- df[-nrow(df),]
  test  <- df[nrow(df),]
  X_train <- train[,-indice]
  y_train <- train[,indice]
  X_test <- test[,-indice]
  y_test <- test[,indice]

  model <- rlasso(
    x = X_train,
    y = y_train,
    post = pl
  )

  pred <- predict(model, newdata = X_test)

  return(list("model" = model,"pred" = pred))
}
```

```{r}
rlasso.rolling.window <- function(Y, test_start,indice=1, pl=FALSE){
  nprev = sum(Y$date >= test_start, na.rm = TRUE)
  save.coef=matrix(NA, nprev, ncol(Y)) #blank matrix for coefficients at each iteration
  save.pred=matrix(NA, nprev, 1) #blank for forecasts
  for(i in nprev:1){ #NB: backwards FOR loop
    Y.window=Y[(1+nprev-i):(nrow(Y)-i),] #define the estimation window (first one: 1 to 491, then 2 to 492 etc.)
    lasso=runrlasso(Y.window,indice,pl) #call the modified function to fit rlasso and predict
    save.coef[(1+nprev-i),]=lasso$model$coef #save estimated coefficients
    save.pred[(1+nprev-i),]=lasso$pred #save the forecast
    cat("iteration",(1+nprev-i),"\n") #display iteration number
  }
  #Some helpful stuff:
  real=Y[,indice] #get actual values
  #plot(real,type="l")
  #lines(c(rep(NA,length(real)-nprev),save.pred),col="red") #padded with NA for blanks, plot predictions vs. actual
  
  rmse=sqrt(mean((tail(real,nprev)-save.pred)^2)) #compute RMSE
  mae=mean(abs(tail(real,nprev)-save.pred)) #compute MAE (Mean Absolute Error)
  errors=c("rmse"=rmse,"mae"=mae) #stack errors in a vector
  
  return(list("pred"=save.pred,"coef"=save.coef,"errors"=errors)) #return forecasts, history of estimated coefficients, and RMSE and MAE for the period.
}
```

```{r bagging}
library(randomForest)
set.seed(759)

MSE <- function(pred, truth){ #start and end body of the function by { } - same as a loop 
  return(mean((truth - pred)^2)) #end function with a return(output) statement. Here we can go straight to return because the object of interest is a simple function of inputs
}

bagging <- function(df, val_start, test_start, indice=1) {
  train = df[df$date < val_start,]
  val = df[df$date >= val_start & df$date < test_start,]
  test = df[df$date >= test_start,]
  
  X_cols <- setdiff(names(train), c("date", "close_usd_per_troy_oz"))
  p <- length(X_cols)
  
  X_train = train[,X_cols]
  y_train = train[,indice]
  X_val = val[,X_cols]
  y_val = val[,indice]
  X_test = test[,X_cols]
  y_test = test[,indice]
  
  ntreev = c(10,500,5000) #vector of tree numbers for looping: try 10, 500 and 5000
  
  nset = length(ntreev) #number of cases for tree numbers - will determine number of iterations in the loop
  
  fmat = matrix(0,nrow(val),nset) #blank matrix for predictions, dimension:sample size by no of cases
  
  #Here we will loop over the tree sizes and produce the bagging fit for each
  for(i in 1:nset) {
    rffit = randomForest(close_usd_per_troy_oz~.,data=train,ntree=ntreev[i], maxnodes=10)
    
    fmat[,i] = predict(rffit, newdata = val) #save each prediction into a separate column of fmat
    cat("Bagging: ntree =", ntreev[i], "\n")
  }
  
  #We plot the OOB error using the largest ntree case to see how it evolves:
  #Plotting the RF object will yield the OOB error plot.
  
  windows()
  par(mfrow=c(1,1)) #1x1 plot
  plot(rffit) #plot the last fitted (largest) OOB error
  
  #Now plot the predicted values:
  oo = order(train$close_usd_per_troy_oz) #ordering for nonlinear plot
  
  rffit2 = randomForest(close_usd_per_troy_oz~.,data=train,ntree=5000, mtry=max(1, floor(p / 3)))
  
  windows()
  plot(rffit2, ylim=c(15,50)) #plot the OOB error
  
  rffit3 = randomForest(close_usd_per_troy_oz~.,data=train,ntree=5000, mtry=p)
  windows()
  plot(rffit3)
  
  #Do the plot of RF vs. bagging:
  xx=seq(1,5000,1)
  windows()
  plot(xx,rffit2$mse, type="l",col="blue", ylim=c(15,50), ylab="OOB MSE", xlab="B", main="Bagging vs. Random forest")
  lines(xx,rffit3$mse, type="l", col="red")
  legend("topright", c("Random Forest, m=7","Bagging"), lty=c(1,1) ,col=c("blue","red"))
  
  #Let's see how bagging does in OOS prediction
  ybag = predict(rffit3,newdata = test)
  
  rmse.bag=sqrt(MSE(test$close_usd_per_troy_oz,ybag)) #compute test RMSE for the tree
}
```
